programs.name: Foundational strength and control
programs.goal: Build the base: single-leg control, hinge and squat patterns, trunk stiffness and shoulder durability before chasing power.
programs.chosenWhen: No movement screen yet, a single-leg squat or overhead squat scored 0-1 of 3, or the athlete is new to lifting.

days.name: Day A
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15

exercises.name: Goblet box squat
exercises.cue: Knees track over toes, sit back to the box

exercises.name: Split squat (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
exercises.cue: Front knee stays stacked, no inward collapse

days.name: Day B
days.focus: Upper body pull, single-leg balance, arm care
days.warmup: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10

programs.progression: Week to week add 1-2 reps per set until the top of the range, then add load and drop back to the bottom of the range. Every fourth week, cut sets by a third.
cautions: Move to Lower-half power only once single-leg squats hold alignment for all reps.

evidence.claim: Single-leg squat compensations are associated with softball pitching pathomechanics in adolescent pitchers.
evidence.source: Friesen et al., Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine, 2021

evidence.claim: Youth without training experience start with low volume and moderate intensity, progressing to 2-4 sets of 6-12 reps once technique is sound.
evidence.source: NSCA Youth Resistance Training position statement

programs.name: Lower-half power and drive
programs.goal: More force into the ground from the drive and stride legs, and faster hip rotation, which is where most windmill velocity comes from.
programs.chosenWhen: Velocity is flat or dropping across PitchLogic sessions, or the athlete has a velocity goal, and the movement screen shows sound single-leg control.

days.name: Day A
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 3 x 3 broad jumps

exercises.name: Lateral bound to stick
exercises.cue: Land soft, hold 2 s, drive-leg push

days.name: Day B
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 3 x 10 m sprints

exercises.name: Side-lying hip external rotation (band or cable)

programs.progression: Keep jumps and bounds at low reps with full rest; add load to deadlift and split squat only when every rep is crisp. Deload every fourth week.
cautions: Schedule Day A at least 48 hours before a hard bullpen.
Skip jumps and bounds on days with lower-body soreness or pain.

evidence.claim: Center-of-mass velocity, ground reaction force, pelvis rotation velocity and body mass explained 57% of the variance in windmill pitch velocity.
evidence.source: Jump et al., Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine, 2026

evidence.claim: Drive-hip external rotation strength was associated with energy flowing out of the trunk and humerus during the pitch.
evidence.source: Friesen et al., Journal of Athletic Training, 2021 (hip ROM, strength and energy flow)

evidence.claim: Ball velocity relates to ground reaction force and to gluteus maximus and medius activity.
evidence.source: Oliver et al., Journal of Sports Sciences, 2011

programs.name: Rotational power and sequencing
programs.goal: Pelvis first, then trunk, then arm: train fast rotation and the trunk stiffness that transfers it, so the arm does less of the work.
programs.chosenWhen: 4D Motion captures are on file (so sequencing can be tracked), velocity is the priority, and single-leg control is sound.

days.name: Day A
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 2 x 5 med ball scoop tosses (light)

days.name: Day B
days.warmup: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10

programs.progression: Med ball work stays light and fast; progress by intent and distance, not ball weight. Add strength-lift load 2.5-5% when all reps feel RPE 7 or easier. Deload every fourth week.
cautions: Stop rotational throws with any low-back pain; replace with anti-rotation holds.

evidence.claim: Because the pitch progresses from pelvis to trunk, variability in pelvis rotation relates to trunk rotation; pelvis rotation rate relates to gluteal activity.
Efficient pelvis-to-trunk energy flow is thought to reduce upper-extremity stress; pitchers with upper-extremity pain showed differences in pelvis and trunk energy flow.
evidence.source: Bordelon et al., American Journal of Sports Medicine, 2022

programs.name: Arm care and scapular durability
programs.goal: Rotator cuff and scapular strength, posterior shoulder mobility and biceps durability for a high-volume underhand motion.
programs.chosenWhen: Throwing-side shoulder internal rotation is well below the glove side, arm soreness is reported, or pitch volume is high (in-season, tournaments). Also added as a secondary block to every program.

days.name: Arm care (10-15 min, most days)
days.warmup: Arm circles x 10 each way, band pull-aparts x 15

exercises.name: Half-kneeling band row to external rotation
Eccentric biceps curl (light, slow 4 s lower)
Sleeper or cross-body stretch (only if cleared by the clinician)

programs.progression: Keep loads light (bands, 1-3 kg). Progress by adding a set or a slower lower, never by going heavy.
cautions: Any shoulder or elbow pain during arm care: stop and tell the coach.
Internal-rotation deficits are flagged for the clinician; the stretch is included only with their okay.

evidence.claim: Loss of shoulder internal rotation was associated with upper-extremity injury risk in high school softball and baseball players.
evidence.source: Shanley et al., American Journal of Sports Medicine, 2011

evidence.claim: The biceps is active through the windmill delivery, a different loading pattern from overhand throwing.
evidence.source: Rojas et al., American Journal of Sports Medicine, 2009

evidence.claim: Shoulder and hip range of motion and strength change across a softball season, so rechecking matters.
evidence.source: Guy et al., International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy, 2021

programs.name: Hip and thoracic mobility
programs.goal: Restore hip rotation and upper-back rotation so the pelvis can open and the trunk can follow without the arm compensating.
programs.chosenWhen: The movement screen shows a hip internal or external rotation gap between sides, or a thoracic rotation gap between sides.

days.name: Mobility circuit (15 min, 3-4 x per week)

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with reach
Deep goblet squat hold with pry

programs.progression: Recheck the movement screen after 4 weeks. Keep the circuit until the side-to-side gap closes, then drop to twice a week.
cautions: Mobility work should never be painful; stop and tell the coach if it is.

evidence.claim: Inadequate hip range of motion and strength may interfere with energy flow through the kinetic chain.
evidence.source: Friesen et al., Journal of Athletic Training, 2021

evidence.claim: Hip and shoulder range-of-motion changes are correlated with injury risk in softball athletes.

programs.name: In-season maintenance
programs.goal: Keep strength and power with the least possible fatigue while games and bullpens carry the load.
programs.chosenWhen: The coach sets the block to in-season.

days.name: Day A (early in the week)
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15

days.name: Day B (optional, 72 h before the next start)
days.warmup: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10

programs.progression: Hold loads steady; the goal is to finish the season as strong as it started. Skip Day B in tournament weeks.
cautions: No lifting within 24 hours before pitching in a game.

evidence.claim: In-season resistance training is typically limited to 1-3 sessions per week, balancing maintenance with recovery.
evidence.source: Hitting Performance Lab, college softball S&C program

evidence.claim: Throwing volume increases should be coordinated so they don't peak at the same time as weight-room loading.

programs.name: Return-to-play (limited clearance)
programs.goal: Keep the rest of the body training around a restriction, within the limits set by the clinician.
programs.chosenWhen: The latest health assessment clears the athlete with limits, or current pain is recorded.

days.name: Day A
days.focus: Lower body and trunk, pain-free only
days.warmup: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15

exercises.name: Goblet box squat (hold the weight only if the arm allows)

programs.progression: Progress only when the clinician updates the restrictions. Nothing here should hurt.
cautions: Nothing that loads the painful area.
Every change goes through the clinician.

evidence.claim: Programs for young athletes should progress conservatively, prioritizing technique and pain-free movement.
evidence.source: NSCA Youth Resistance Training position statement

pitchLimitSource.label: STOP Sports Injuries / AOSSM fastpitch pitching recommendations, as summarized in Kamarajugadda et al., Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine, 2023
